public_rationale: The experimental evidence runs against distraction when measured as public concern: catastrophic narratives did not diminish concern about immediate harms. But Marcus did not confine his claim to that measure. These experiments do not settle whether media coverage or policy resources were displaced. A broad verdict would therefore depend on an audience and measure he did not specify.
limitations: The two items describe one study.
Short experimental exposure cannot establish the long-term effects of sustained advocacy.
The source's wording leaves the institutional scope open.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is a recurring displacement of attention to present harms by speculative catastrophic-AI narratives.
Underplayed is assessed as receiving less attention because of those narratives, rather than against an evaluator's preferred level of concern.
Relevant attention includes public concern, media coverage, and policy priorities; the source does not select one.
Tend to describes a general tendency, not a conditional forecast or a claim that every audience responds identically.
The causal account concerns discourse up to the post date; no fixed measurement window is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Representative longitudinal, experimental, or decision-level evidence shows that catastrophic-AI narratives reduced attention to immediate LLM harms across relevant settings.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence covering the claimed settings consistently shows no meaningful displacement, or increased attention to immediate harms following exposure to catastrophic narratives.
